questions.q: What are the three real Workflow state values an article moves through on its way to being visible to end users?
options: Draft, Review, Published
New, Assigned, Resolved
Open, Pending, Closed
Submitted, Escalated, Approved
questions.explain: Draft, Review, and Published form the publishing path; Retired is a later, separate state covered in Lesson 20.

questions.q: Why is the approval gate between Review and Published a real quality-control mechanism, not just bureaucracy?
options: Without it, a subtly wrong or outdated article can go live and spread inaccurate guidance across hundreds of articles and thousands of readers
The gate exists only to slow authors down with no actual benefit
ServiceNow technically requires an approval before any record can change state
It has no effect on article accuracy, only on publishing speed
questions.explain: At scale, an unreviewed inaccurate article doesn't just mislead one reader — other agents start citing it as fact.

questions.q: How is the Draft-Review-Published approval gate actually implemented?
options: A Flow Designer flow triggers on Workflow state changing to Review and uses an Ask for Approval action routed to a Knowledge manager or SME
It can only be enforced by a System Administrator manually changing each record
ACLs alone block the Published state with no flow involved
It requires a custom scripted REST integration outside the platform
questions.explain: Knowledge Management reuses the same Flow Designer approval mechanism covered for change requests and other record flows.

questions.q: What happens when a reviewer rejects an article submitted for approval?
options: The flow routes it back to Workflow state Draft, with the reviewer's comments attached for the original author to act on
The article is immediately deleted from the Knowledge Base
The article is published anyway, with a warning banner
Nothing changes; the article stays in Review indefinitely
questions.explain: Rejection returns the article to Draft with specific feedback, rather than leaving it stuck or silently discarding it.

questions.q: Who does a well-implemented approval flow route a Review-state article to?
options: Any end user who happens to read the Self-Service Knowledge Base
A Knowledge manager or a subject-matter expert for that Knowledge Base's Category
The original author, to approve their own submission
The ServiceNow platform administrator by default, regardless of subject matter
questions.explain: Routing to a Knowledge manager or SME ensures the person approving actually has the expertise to catch inaccuracies.
